teams.heading: Former Bulls colleagues tip Jake White's Fiji to surprise people
teams.body: Jake White's former Bulls colleagues believe Fiji have appointed the right man, and Chris Rossouw, his former backline coach, says he "wouldn't be surprised if they're going to surprise people." White, 62, was chosen from 31 applicants and takes charge against Japan, before Nations Championship games against France, Ireland and Italy.

lead.why: The other candidates have already run, so this is the fresh angle on the White appointment, with Fiji's first match under him and the November schedule.

teams.heading: Tom Pearson back training as England quartet eye Saints return
teams.body: Northampton's Tom Pearson is back training with the full squad, and Phil Dowson says "it won't be long before he's back out there", though there is no confirmation he will be ready for Saturday's match against Leicester. The bigger boost for England is that Manny Iyogun, Alex Coles, Henry Pollock and Tommy Freeman, rested for the Champions Cup win over Cardiff, are all expected back this weekend. Dowson also has a hard call at scrum-half between Alex Mitchell and Archie McParland.

lead.why: It is the highest-scoring new item and links a Northampton update directly to four England players expected back this weekend.

teams.heading: Thomas Ramos to miss France's entire autumn Nations Championship with thigh injury
teams.body: France lose their main goal kicker for the autumn. Thomas Ramos will miss all four Nations Championship matches after aggravating a thigh injury first picked up in September, according to L'Equipe, and France have chosen to rest him rather than risk a longer problem. The fullback, Six Nations top scorer four years running, is also a loss against a backdrop of injuries to Matthieu Jalibert, Emmanuel Meafou and Julien Marchand. Galthié is expected to name his 42-man squad on Wednesday.

lead.why: A men's national-team availability blow for France's entire autumn campaign, which outranks the club and pundit items on offer.

teams.heading: Farrell to name Ireland squad today with Caelan Doris still sidelined
teams.body: Andy Farrell names his Ireland squad for the second Nations Championship window on Wednesday, and captain Caelan Doris is still sidelined, though some welcome returnees are expected. Ireland are fourth in the Northern Hemisphere table behind France, Scotland and England, and Farrell is expected to demand a notable uplift in accuracy and energy after the error-strewn July defeat by New Zealand in Auckland. Argentina, Fiji and South Africa come next.

lead.why: Farrell's squad announcement is the most significant new men's national-team story in today's shortlist, and the only one that is a direct selection event.

teams.heading: Italy lost 32-14 to South Africa at home in November 2025
teams.body: Italy's most recent meeting with South Africa was a 32-14 defeat at home in November 2025, in the International Friendlies. This is a single result, not a head-to-head record. The next fixture brings the sides together again in Round 4 of the Nations Championship, with Italy on no wins from three matches, having scored 37 points and conceded 131 in that span.

teams.heading: Former Scotland captain Stuart Hogg has MBE stripped over domestic abuse conviction
teams.body: Stuart Hogg, who won 100 Scotland caps and toured three times with the British & Irish Lions, had his MBE cancelled in March after pleading guilty to a domestic abuse charge involving his estranged wife. The honour, awarded in the 2024 New Year Honours for services to rugby, was removed from the official register. He is one of 15 people to lose honours in 2026, and was handed a one-year community payback order in January 2025.

lead.why: The strongest men's Scotland item not already run, and the only one in the shortlist about a men's player rather than the women's side or Ritchie's club debut.

teams.heading: Tandy won't rule out Faletau from World Cup despite November squad omission
teams.body: Steve Tandy has not ruled out Taulupe Faletau for the 2027 World Cup, even though the 35-year-old was left out of the November squad. Faletau, who has 109 Wales caps and has not played under Tandy, only returned from injury in Cardiff's Champions Cup defeat by Northampton on Sunday. Tandy said "we would definitely not rule anyone out", but has made clear the decision depends on Faletau putting together consistent rugby first.

lead.why: It is the freshest new item, with Tandy's own comments on Faletau's World Cup prospects after his omission from the 39-man squad.

teams.heading: Argentina-led four-nation bid for 2035 World Cup awaits World Rugby decision
teams.body: Argentina lead a joint bid with Uruguay, Chile and Brazil to host the 2035 Rugby World Cup, and the bid stays open until World Rugby selects the host. Reuters reported the submission on 6 October, and Planet Rugby frames the bid as a challenge to the governing body's reported desire for a European return. The host is still to be chosen, so the Pumas' hosting case remains unresolved.

teams.heading: Wallabies slip to seventh in world rankings, behind Scotland, after Bledisloe losses
teams.body: Australia are now seventh in the World Rugby rankings, having dropped below Scotland after back-to-back Bledisloe Cup defeats to New Zealand. Those are the first two losses of the Les Kiss era, which ended an unbeaten run featuring wins over Japan, Argentina and South Africa, and the scorelines were 50-19 at Eden Park and 43-21 in Sydney. The slide lands ahead of the England Test at Twickenham and next year's home World Cup.

lead.why: A new ranking consequence of the Bledisloe losses that the Australian side has not yet had reported, and it reframes the England Test.

teams.heading: Japan's women's sevens defend ARESS title; Greening's men beat Hong Kong China
teams.body: Japan's women's sevens side finished the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series with an undefeated campaign in Colombo, beating China 14-7 in the final to take the series with the maximum 40 points. The men also won the Leg 2 final, 28-14 over Series winners Hong Kong China, a rare defeat for the Hong Kong side. Phil Greening, Japan men's sevens head coach, said the win was valuable because it 'demonstrates the team's ability to adapt to different situations.'

lead.why: The only Japan item not already run, and the Smith and league-rules stories have both been covered.

teams.heading: Kieran Read sees Damian McKenzie back at full-back once Mo'unga returns
teams.body: Damian McKenzie's spell at No. 10 may be temporary. Justin Marshall says the 31-year-old has "massively elevated himself" over two Bledisloe Cup starts at fly-half, but expects the November Tests against Scotland, Wales and England to test him harder on wetter UK ground against static ball. Kieran Read expects McKenzie back at full-back once Richie Mo'unga, recovering from a calf injury, is fit. McKenzie moved to fly-half after injuries to Mo'unga and Ruben Love.

lead.why: It is the strongest new item on the shortlist and gives a fan a concrete selection question about McKenzie's role at 10 and 15.

teams.heading: Springbok Dan du Preez out for considerable time with hamstring tear
teams.body: Dan du Preez has suffered a hamstring tear in training that will keep the Springbok back-rower out for a considerable amount of time, according to Bath head of rugby Johann van Graan. The 31-year-old, who joined Bath from Sale Sharks this season, missed their Investec Champions Cup defeat to Montpellier and will also miss the next two Premiership matches. Bath are already without Sam Underhill until December following bicep surgery.

lead.why: A new injury to a Springbok forward, with the club's own head of rugby giving the timeframe, is harder news than the pundit commentary and the rest of the shortlist.
